Scar Pattern Index (Clarkson et al. 2006)

Source: R/stats.R
compute_spi.Rd

Computes the Scar Pattern Index of one core: the length of the resultant of its scar directions divided by the number of scars, from 0 (directions cancel out) to 1 (all scars run the same way). By default the function returns three readings:

Usage

compute_spi(
  dx,
  dy,
  dz,
  lengths = NULL,
  raw = TRUE,
  rarefied = TRUE,
  random_interval = TRUE,
  m = 3,
  max_comb = 2000,
  seed = 2226
)

Arguments

dx, dy, dz

Numeric vectors of equal length: the X, Y and Z components of the scar direction vectors of one core, for example End_X - Start_X etc., or the d_x, d_y, d_z columns returned by align_scar_batch(). The vectors are normalised to unit length inside the function; rows of zero length or with missing values are left out.

lengths

Optional numeric vector of scar lengths, one per vector. If given, each unit direction is weighted by its length, reproducing the length-weighted SPI of Clarkson et al. (2006). The rarefied value and the random interval are defined for unweighted SPI only and are NA when lengths is given.

raw

Logical. Return the raw SPI (SPI_raw)? Default TRUE.

rarefied

Logical. Return the rarefied SPI (SPI_rarefied)? Default TRUE.

random_interval

Logical. Return the random interval at the core's scar count (SPI_lower, SPI_upper) and the position of the raw SPI relative to it (SPI_vs_random)? Default TRUE.

m

Number of scars per combination for the rarefied value. Default 3.

max_comb

Largest number of combinations averaged. Above it, max_comb distinct combinations are drawn at random (a Monte Carlo approximation of the mean over all combinations). Default 2000.

seed

Seed for that random draw; the caller's random stream is restored afterwards. NULL draws from the current stream. Default 2226.

Value

A one-row tibble with n_scar (the number of scars used) and the columns selected by raw, rarefied and random_interval: SPI_raw, SPI_rarefied, SPI_lower, SPI_upper and SPI_vs_random ("within" or "outside"). All values are NA for cores with fewer than three scars.

Details

  • raw SPI, computed from all scars together;

  • rarefied SPI, the mean SPI over every combination of m scars (Xiao et al., in prep.). Its expectation does not change with the scar count, so it is the value to use when comparing cores or groups of cores;

  • the random interval at the core's scar count: the central 95% of the SPI of cores whose scar directions are uniform on the sphere, and whether the raw SPI lies "within" or "outside" it.

Which value for which question. Raw SPI shifts with the scar count: the fewer the scars, the less their directions cancel out, even when they are random. A single core is therefore judged by comparing its raw SPI with the random interval at its own scar count; cores and groups of cores are compared with the rarefied SPI, whose expectation does not depend on the scar count (Xiao et al., in prep.).

Reading the random interval. SPI above the upper bound indicates scar directions more concentrated on one side than random directions produce at this scar count. SPI below the lower bound is typical of opposed (bidirectional) flaking, whose two sets of removals cancel out. A value "within" the interval cannot be told apart from random directions at this scar count. See random_interval().

Changes in 0.2.0. The function returns a one-row tibble instead of a single number, and normalises the input vectors itself: raw displacement vectors (end minus start) now give the unweighted SPI, and the length-weighted SPI is requested with lengths.

References

Clarkson, C., Vinicius, L., & Lahr, M. M. (2006). Quantifying flake scar patterning on cores using 3D recording techniques. Journal of Archaeological Science, 33(1), 132–142.

Bretzke, K., & Conard, N. J. (2012). Evaluating morphological variability in lithic assemblages using 3D models of stone artifacts. Journal of Archaeological Science, 39(12), 3741–3749.

Hurlbert, S. H. (1971). The nonconcept of species diversity: a critique and alternative parameters. Ecology, 52(4), 577–586.

See also

compute_ei(), spi_ei_batch(), random_interval(), compute_spi_angle()

Examples

# Twelve scars running broadly the same way
set.seed(1)
d <- matrix(rnorm(36, sd = 0.4), 12, 3)
d[, 1] <- d[, 1] + 1
compute_spi(d[, 1], d[, 2], d[, 3])
#> # A tibble: 1 × 6
#>   n_scar SPI_raw SPI_rarefied SPI_lower SPI_upper SPI_vs_random
#>    <int>   <dbl>        <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl> <chr>        
#> 1     12   0.902        0.929    0.0790     0.500 outside      

# Raw SPI only
compute_spi(d[, 1], d[, 2], d[, 3], rarefied = FALSE, random_interval = FALSE)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 2
#>   n_scar SPI_raw
#>    <int>   <dbl>
#> 1     12   0.902

# Length-weighted SPI (Clarkson et al. 2006)
compute_spi(d[, 1], d[, 2], d[, 3], lengths = runif(12, 5, 30),
            rarefied = FALSE, random_interval = FALSE)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 2
#>   n_scar SPI_raw
#>    <int>   <dbl>
#> 1     12   0.918
